newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economy at the bottom of cycle - Bolger.
newsitem.headline: NZ economy at the bottom of cycle - Bolger.

text.p: The economy is at the bottom of its business cycle, prime minister Jim Bolger said in an interview with Radio New Zealand on Wednesday.
"Certainly the New Zealand economy, every commentator has said, is going through the bottom of the business cycle. That happens from time to time, it always does in every country.
"What's different this time is that the bottom of the business cycle is much higher than the average growth rate in the previous economy," Bolger said.
Bolger said the upcoming budget would demonstrate clearly leadership on matters of importance to the business community.
In putting together the coalition agreement, National and NZ First had formed a clear idea of the business environment the parties wanted to create.
"That will be reflected in the statements contained in the budget. We do know that you have to have a strong economy if you're going to deliver strong social policy," he said.
Bolger said a joint caucus meeting between the coalition partners on Tuesday night, called to organise strategy before next week's budget, had gone well.
"The presentation by the treasurer (Winston Peters) and the minister of finance (Bill Birch), was exceptionally well-received," he said.
It was only the second joint caucus between the two parties since the coalition was formed.
The budget is due on June 26.
